meta.note: Cluster-level adjudication of duplicate/overlap questions raised row-by-row by ukraine-gas/{ref-sweep-operating,annual,cancelled-review}, the GulfPub + OSM recons and the source survey. Read-and-flag only; no edits staged. READ THIS FIRST — TWO geometry rules govern Ukraine and they pull in opposite directions. (1) Most Ukrainian gas routes are 2-5 vertex SCHEMATICS, so a drawn span is a LOWER BOUND on corridor extent: a drawn-vs-stated gap proves nothing unless the drawn span EXCEEDS the stated length by a wide margin (it does in exactly two places — P0784, 759.1 km drawn against 164.00 km stated, and P1481, whose 333.00 km cannot span an Ananiv-Bohorodchany corridor that is ~424 km great-circle). (2) IDENTICAL DRAWN GEOMETRY IS NOT EVIDENCE OF DUPLICATION — parallel Soviet strings share one right-of-way trace, the same convention Kazakhstan carries. THREE of the eight clusters REFUTE a duplicate hypothesis (F, G, H), recorded deliberately so the next sweep does not re-raise them; two CONFIRM one (A, E) and two are PARTIAL_OVERLAP (B, D). Ukraine's own method lesson is that ONLY SOURCING DECIDES: cluster G looked like a textbook double count (two rows, one corridor, both 292.00 km, both 29.00 bcm/y) and the duplicate is still REFUTED, because UTG's chronology names 'Ivatsevychi-Dolyna (I nytka)' 1976 at 357.7 km and '(II nytka)' 1977 at 366.7 km as two physically distinct 1220 mm strings — while simultaneously falsifying BOTH of GEM's numbers, since 292.00 km matches neither string and 29.00 bcm/y is the SYSTEM total restated twice (GEM's own note says so; ISANS 2023 puts the corridor near 30). A refuted duplicate is therefore not a clean row. The country's two cross-cutting defects, both escalated: GAZPROM ATTRIBUTED OWNERSHIP OF UKRAINIAN PIPE (P1485, P0783, P0775 at 48.6%, P0776 at 'Gazprom 100%' beside a second co-owner) — Gazprom owns no Ukrainian section, the post-2019 unbundling put the GTS under GTSOU; and SYSTEM/AGGREGATE CAPACITY RESTATED AS A LINE'S OWN (P0784's 24.00 bcm/y is verbatim an aggregate over three threads that double-counts capacity P0786 already carries; both G rows at 29.00), the same shape India and Kazakhstan carry. ON THE OWNERSHIP DEFECT, READ THE NARROW VERSION, NOT THE BROAD ONE: a full-tab count run 2026-08-15 puts Gazprom in `Owner` on 20 of the 47 rows, and for 14 of them the unweighted pair 'Gazprom PJSC; Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' on a genuinely transnational Russia+Ukraine row is the DEFENSIBLE convention, not a defect — so the earlier reading that P0783 is an instance is WITHDRAWN. What survives is two narrow classes. (i) A percentage of [100.%] recorded alongside a second named owner, which is arithmetically impossible and is NOT Gazprom-specific — P0768 and P0776 put Gazprom at 100% beside GTSOU, and P0761 puts GTSOU at 100% beside Gazprom AND QazaqGaz. That is a notation question for a human: if [100.%] is meant as '100% of the section in that party's own country' the convention needs stating, and if it is meant as a share of the whole line all three cells are wrong. (ii) A sole non-Ukrainian owner on a row that lists Ukraine — P0791 (Gazprom; QazaqGaz), P0793, P1471, P2387 and P1485 (all Gazprom PJSC [100.%]), plus P5935 (Moldovatransgaz [100.%]). P1485 is the unambiguous one, because its CountriesOrAreas is Ukraine ALONE. Separately P1487 still names Ukrtransgaz, the pre-2020 entity. Cluster A confirms P0777 and P1480 are one system — the Soviet KZU, a documented two-string build — and it is ALSO this pass's own correction, so read the corrected version: the operator's construction chronology became readable through Wayback after the cluster was first adjudicated and gives the two strings as 183.6 km/∅1020 mm (1970) and 216.3 km/∅1220 mm (1972), summing to exactly P1480's 399.90 km. The 367 + 506 = 873 km pair this leg first called 'the only verifiable figures' is WITHDRAWN — it is a uk.wikipedia figure attributed to that same chronology page, which contains neither number, and the page was already saved into the run directory when the cluster was written. So P1480's length is SOURCED and should be carried onto the surviving row; P0777's 1,112.00 km is the unsourced one (its VTG citation is a genuine 404), and may be a conflation with the upstream Yefremivka-Dolyna-Kyiv trunk that the chronology says KZU continues. Unchanged: P1480's Drozdovychi endpoint is anachronistic (it belongs to the older Komarno-Drozdovychi corridor and the post-2006 Poland interconnection, not to the 1970s KZU). The method lesson is narrow and worth carrying: an UNRESOLVED written while a source was unreachable must be revisited when access returns — and a figure a secondary article attributes to a primary document is not that document's figure until the document says it. Cluster E is confirmed at MEDIUM only: P5989 minus P7817+P7818 leaves 99.30 km against a reported '>100 km' new Berdyansk-Melitopol section, but every source is Russian state or occupation media tracing to one July 2022 directive, so the arithmetic is stronger than the sourcing. Cluster C stays UNRESOLVED because no source says whether ACHB is P1485's western half or a separate parallel string. TWO OPEN QUESTIONS THAT NEED A HUMAN: the Ivatsevychi corridor may be a THREE-string system — this pass's own evidence file describes Torzhok-Ivatsevychi-Dolyna with three strings while cluster G sourced Ivatsevychi-Dolyna with two, which are different corridors, so whether GEM is missing a string is still open and belongs to Discovery, not here; and P0775/P0776's 298.00/297.00 km near-coincidence is unexplained even though the duplicate is refuted (Gazprom's own 65 vs 45 Mm3/day table converts to 23.725/16.425 bcm/y, matching GEM almost exactly, which makes it GEM's likely ORIGIN rather than corroboration). Three load-bearing sources could not be read in this pass and are NOT deletions: utg.ua's chronology and tsoua.com both 403 behind the operator's WAF, and moldovatransgaz.md fails TLS (its mtg.md mirror is staged instead) — the UTG chronology is the source that would settle clusters A and C.

Standing practice in this repo is to REPOINT a ref to its archived capture, not to treat the content as unsourced; the figures are sourceable, they are simply misread (below). VTG groups four lines under one 'Система газопроводов' block with a rowspan'd name cell, and the sub-names map in order to the data rows: Шебелинка-Полтава-Київ = 700 mm / 438 km, Єфремівка-Диканька-Київ = 1000 mm / 477.8 km, Шебелинка-Диканька-Київ = 1000 mm / 522 km, and Київ-Захід України = 1000,1200 mm / 590 km, 1 нитка. That is a documented conflation, not an unexplained number, so the fix is a scope statement in ResearcherNotes alongside the smaller value, exactly as this recommendation anticipated. (3) Note for whoever applies it: VTG's own КЗУ figure is 590 km on ONE string, against UTG's 183.6 + 216.3 = 399.90 km on two. The operator's construction chronology is the better source and 399.90 stands; record the 590 as a documented second-source tension rather than resolving it silently. Reading any single number off this table without checking its rowspan grouping is the trap — the same block structure puts three separate lines under 'Північний Кавказ-Центр'.

Sources checked and verified live: kommersant.ru/doc/5459063 (2022-07-13, 'Российский газ дотянется до Запорожья' — states the >100 km Berdyansk-Melitopol figure and the two-part restore+extend plan, and that the old corridor 'was partially unused since the 2009 gas conflict' i.e. needs partial not full rebuild); ria.ru/20220719/gazoprovod-1803530880.html (2022-07-19 — Zaporizhzhia occupation head Yevgeny Balitsky announces the Berdyansk-Melitopol build, no length given); ria.ru/20221025/gaz-1826622360.html (2022-10-25 — gas reaches Berdyansk first, per occupation figure Vladimir Rogov, with Melitopol to follow); neftegaz.ru's follow-up (2022-10-31, gas begins flowing to Melitopol households) corroborates the completion date range but the page is JS-rendered and its live text could not be extracted for a substring check — cite with that caveat if used. All of the above ultimately trace to ONE Russian government decision (Deputy PM Khusnullin's July 2022 directive) reported through aligned state/occupation channels — this is single-origin, medium tier by the standing rule, not two independent origins. Owner/attribution flag: P5989 carries a blank Owner while 'operating'. No source names a specific legal operator for the restored/extended line — occupation-administration statements attribute oversight to Russia's Ministry of Energy (Minenergo) as the sponsoring federal body, not a named pipeline operator, and Gazprom is documented (neftegaz 2014 reporting) as the historical owner of the original 1950s Taganrog-Mariupol trunk only, before its 2009 closure — that attribution does not automatically carry to a post-2022 occupation-built asset. GEM should NOT default Owner to either the Gas TSO of Ukraine (which does not operate in occupied territory) or Gazprom (unsourced for this specific restored/extended asset) — leave Owner blank and document the ambiguity in ResearcherNotes rather than guessing.

Two independent, non-GEM sources each name «Єлець—Курськ—Диканька» and «Єлець—Курськ—Київ» as separate 1220 mm trunk lines: (1) the Kursk Oblast district administration's official gas-corridor/security-zone listing (kurskr.rkursk.ru, archived 2022-05-19 at web.archive.org/web/20220519195206/http://kurskr.rkursk.ru/index.php?sub_menus_id=18020&id_mat=2996) states verbatim: '...Уренгой – Ужгород Ф1420мм, Елец – Курск – Диканька Ф1220мм, Елец – Курск – Киев Ф1220мм...' as two items in a corridor list, both 1220 mm — i.e. a Russian government body, independent of Gazprom, distinguishing them by name while giving them the SAME diameter, which rules out 'different diameter = different line, same diameter = the same line' as a shortcut; naming is what does the work here. (2) Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own Kurskoe LPUMG page (moskva-tr.gazprom.ru/kurskoe-lpumg/, archived 2025-05-12) states in its historical-construction narrative: 'строятся магистральные газопроводы: «Елец — Курск — Киев», «Уренгой — Ужгород», «Елец — Курск — Диканька», «Елец — Кременчуг — Кривой Рог», магистральный газопровод «Прогресс»' — again both named as separate items in a list of distinct Soviet-era trunks built through the oblast. (3) uk.wikipedia's own dedicated article on «Єлець — Курськ — Диканька» (cites Kursk oblast admin, the Ukrtransgaz chronology, and two independent Lipetsk/Kursk regional gas-supply characterization documents) gives 1220 mm, 5.5 MPa, commissioned 1984 — matching GEM P0775's diameter and StartYear1 exactly. That is the geometric signature of two lines sharing an origin/transit corridor, not one line recorded twice. CAPACITY (weaker, treat as single-origin, not independent corroboration): the live moskva-tr.gazprom.ru Kurskoe LPUMG page (fetched once successfully via curl with a browser UA on 2026-08-15; the site subsequently became intermittently unreachable to both direct fetch and archive.org's Save-Page-Now, which returned 523 origin-unreachable — this is a live-site availability problem, not a dead-link finding, and I could not get url_verifier.py to pass on the live URL for that reason) lists 'Елец-Курск-Диканька» диаметр трубы 1220 мм ... производительность 65 млн. м3/сут' and 'Елец-Курск-Киев» диаметр трубы 1220 мм ... производительность 45 млн. м3/сут'. 65 and 45 million m3/day annualize to 23.725 and 16.425 bcm/y — matching GEM's stated 23.73 and 16.43 bcm/y on P0775/P0776 almost to the decimal. That precision match is too exact to be coincidence, but it cuts the other way on independence: it suggests this same characteristics document (or a shared upstream) may be the actual origin of GEM's own capacity figures, so it should NOT be counted as a second independent source validating the capacity VALUES — only as further confirmation that the two lines are tracked as separate items with separate capacities. P1453 (Yefremivka-Dykanka-Kyiv) is documented in kzu_evidence.md as part of the 1970 KZU-1 commissioning cohort, a third distinct line converging on the same Dykanka hub — consistent with Dykanka being a genuine multi-line junction, not evidence that any of these rows duplicate each other.
